**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject every recognized foreign-currency marker**

Reject the full foreign-currency vocabulary here, not only this abbreviated list. Values such as `四万元港幣`, `新台币1000元`, or `加拿大元1000元` currently normalize to exact RMB amounts, so `canonicalMonetaryExpression` equates them with RMB gold labels. Although source review later removes the calculation amount, `assessCase` scores the accepted representation itself, causing both raw and accepted experiment metrics to award false true positives for foreign-currency predictions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Collapse nested spans from the same anchored event**

Treat overlapping equivalent spans in the same uniquely located quote as one event. For example, if the model emits otherwise identical candidates with values `人民币四万元` and `四万元` from one quote, both normalize to `40000.00` but receive different `sourceLocation` ranges and are retained. This reintroduces duplicate candidates for a single fact and produces an extra false positive in the event-based scorer, while still allowing genuinely separate occurrences at distinct non-overlapping positions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject qualified prefixes before a matched amount**

Do not accept a valid numeric suffix when the preceding text changes its semantics. Inputs such as `数十万元` and `几十万元` currently match the internal `十万元` token and become exact `100000.00`, while `负数四万元` matches `四万元` and becomes positive `40000.00`; the boundary check only examines the final character before the token, and the candidate-level checks inspect outside the entire value, so neither layer corrects these cases. This makes approximate or explicitly negative evidence exact and also lets the scorer equate it with a positive RMB gold amount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not treat lexical 元 and 圆 as currency units**

Require `元` or `圆` to occur in a monetary context before classifying the value as monetary. A model-produced money candidate such as `2024年元月工资`, `元月份工资`, or `元旦工资` currently takes this branch solely because it contains `元`, so runtime ingestion accepts it instead of applying the new no-amount rejection used for `2024年7月工资`; unrelated text such as `圆满完成工资发放` is affected similarly. These candidates remain visible with `amount: null` and distort accepted/rejected coverage even though they contain no monetary expression.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve ranges whose second endpoint repeats the currency**

When a range repeats an explicit currency marker, such as a candidate value `人民币3万元` inside `人民币3万元至人民币4万元`, the suffix check does not recognize the range because it requires a numeral immediately after `至`. The candidate consequently remains `exact` with amount `30000.00`, and the later source review also accepts it, allowing a cropped range endpoint to become a usable exact amount. Permit RMB markers between the range connector and the second endpoint.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict event containment to permitted value expansions**

A candidate can use an entire narrative paragraph as its `value` and still receive a true positive merely because that span contains the event anchor. For example, `王甲声称公司长期拖欠其工资，现要求支付4000元并追究责任。` normalizes to `4000.00`, aligns with the `4000元` anchor through this containment branch, and receives a TP in all six raw/accepted modes despite violating the amount-fragment contract. Limit super-spans to the explicitly permitted currency, noun, or date-boundary expansions rather than accepting arbitrary text around an anchor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exempt relative wage months from rate detection**

The calendar exemption only recognizes a digit or Chinese numeral before `月工资`, so ordinary wage-period phrases such as `王甲上月工资1000元`, `本月工资1000元`, or `下月工资1000元` are classified as monthly-rate contexts. A non-rate candidate for the explicit `1000元` is therefore downgraded to `rate_unit_mismatch` with `amount: null`, even when its `period` correctly names that relative month. Treat the relative-month words supported by the extraction prompt as calendar boundaries as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve duplicates whose source position is ambiguous**

When an otherwise identical quote occurs multiple times, both candidates have `occurrence === null`, but this fallback still treats matching fallback data as proof that they are duplicates. For example, two `四万元` candidates against `第一次支付四万元。第二次支付四万元。` are both source-ambiguous and could represent the two distinct payments, yet the second is rejected. Only collapse candidates when a unique overlapping occurrence was established; ambiguous observations need to remain available for review.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject no-amount descriptions for every supported relative month**

The relative-period vocabulary here omits forms that the new source-rate logic explicitly supports, including `这个月`, `这月`, `当月`, `该月`, `上个月`, and `下一个月`. Consequently, a model-produced money candidate such as `这个月工资` is classified as `undetermined` rather than `not_monetary`, so runtime ingestion accepts it despite there being no amount or unknown-amount marker. Include these definite wage-period forms in the no-amount classification.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict nested deduplication to permitted amount wrappers**

Fresh evidence in runtime ingestion shows that this containment test considers any exact-value super-span equivalent to its nested amount, without applying the scorer's finite-wrapper restriction. If the model emits `王甲声称公司应支付四万元工资` before a valid `四万元` candidate with the same attributes, the latter is rejected and only the narrative value remains; the corrected event scorer then refuses to align that narrative value, turning a valid accepted prediction into a false negative based solely on output order. Limit containment deduplication to the permitted currency/noun wrappers, or retain the valid minimal span.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not discard multipliers attached to the matched amount**

When a multiplier follows the monetary token, this replacement removes it as though it were an unrelated count. Consequently, `normalizeMoneyValueV4('四万元的2倍')` returns `exact` with `40000.00`, even though the expression requires arithmetic and must not be represented by its base operand. Preserve unrelated counts such as headcounts, but classify an attached `倍` expression as unsupported rather than exposing the wrong exact amount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject source currencies separated by attribution words**

Fresh evidence in the current tree shows that a minimal `四万元` candidate from `王甲的工资以港币支付四万元` is accepted with `amount: "40000.00"` and `status: "exact"`. This guard recognizes only currency markers directly adjoining the amount, so ordinary attribution phrases such as `港币工资四万元`, `工资以港币支付四万元`, and `港币计价工资四万元` bypass it; the new lowercase-Chinese parser then represents a foreign-currency value as exact RMB. Extend the anchored check to finite same-event currency-attribution wording without crossing clause boundaries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject multipliers linked through wage nouns**

Fresh evidence after the multiplier fix shows that the bridge intentionally excludes wage nouns, so `四万元工资的2倍`, `四万元基本工资的2倍`, and a cropped `四万元` from those source phrases still normalize to exact `40000.00`. Because the remaining `2倍` is later discarded as an allowed count, runtime ingestion retains the operand as an exact amount rather than an unsupported expression. Permit a finite set of directly attached amount nouns before `的…倍`, while continuing to stop at punctuation or unrelated prose.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize rate labels before accepting lowercase totals**

With the newly supported lowercase amount, a mislabeled total candidate for `四万元` in `王甲月工资标准为四万元`, `王甲月薪标准：四万元`, or `王甲每月基本工资四万元` now survives this source-unit check as exact `40000.00`. `sourceRateUnit` only permits a short list of tokens immediately after `月工资`/`月薪`, so common rate words such as `标准`, `基本`, and `约定为` prevent it from detecting the monthly rate and applying `rate_unit_mismatch`. Extend the finite rate-prefix grammar to cover these explicit wage-standard constructions while retaining the calendar-month exemptions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Terminate the whole Worker process tree before restarting**

The built-in restart scenario calls this helper and proceeds as soon as the Wrangler parent emits `exit`, but `child.kill()` signals only that parent and does not establish that its launcher/workerd descendants have closed. The cancellation runner changed in this same commit uses a detached process group and waits for `close` specifically because parent exit can precede descendant teardown; here, a surviving descendant can keep the disposable D1 state or Wrangler sockets active while the next Worker starts, making the required HTTP regression flaky and allowing final cleanup to report success with an orphan still running. Apply the same process-group and close-wait teardown to this runner.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject relative-day wage descriptions without amounts**

Extend the definite wage-period grammar to relative days such as `今日工资`, `当日工资`, `昨日工资`, and `当天工资`. These values do not match `wageStage`, and the fallback leaves their day qualifier behind, so `classifyMonetaryExpression` returns `undetermined`; `validateRuntimeCandidateOutput` consequently accepts them as money candidates instead of using the no-amount rejection path, inflating accepted coverage with descriptions that contain no monetary expression.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exempt relative-day wage periods from rate detection**

Handle relative-day prefixes before interpreting `日工资` as a daily rate. In the runtime ingestion path, a correct total from source text such as `王甲今日工资合计四万元` matches the `日工资` prefix, but `calendarPrefix` ends in `今`, so the numeric calendar exemption does not apply and this month-only exemption is skipped; `sourceUnitMismatch` then downgrades the exact amount to `rate_unit_mismatch` with `amount: null`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject currencies linked by bare valuation verbs**

Fresh evidence after the earlier attribution fix: when the source says `王甲的工资以港币计四万元` and the model crops both `value` and `quote` to `四万元`, the bridge fails because bare `计` (and likewise `计算`/`折算`) is absent from this vocabulary. `validateRuntimeCandidateOutput` consequently retains `amount: "40000.00"` with `status: "exact"`, representing an HKD amount as RMB; extend the finite bridge to cover these same-event valuation constructions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject formulas with nonnumeric operands**

When an attached operator is followed by a named factor rather than a numeric literal, this pattern does not recognize the expression. For example, both `normalizeMoneyValueV4('四万元乘以出勤系数')` and a cropped `四万元` candidate from that source remain exact `40000.00`, although four万元 is only the base operand and the result is unknown; recognize finite symbolic operands after explicit operators so these formulas cannot expose their base amount as exact.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize conjunction-based range endpoints**

When a range is written as `工资在3万元和4万元之间` or `介于3万元与4万元`, a model candidate cropped to the first `3万元` bypasses both source range checks because `和`/`与…之间` is not part of `RANGE_LINK`. Runtime ingestion then preserves an exact `30000.00` endpoint even though the source supplies only a range; add an explicitly bounded conjunction-range form that requires the closing `之间` to avoid confusing ordinary lists with ranges.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse Arabic digits in jiao and fen suffixes**

The new token grammar permits only Chinese single digits after `元`, so ordinary exact literals such as `5元5角` and `5元5角2分` are classified as `unsupported` with no amount, while their Chinese-digit and decimal equivalents normalize to `5.50` and `5.52`. Include Arabic digits in the `角`/`分` suffix grammar and parse the complete token so valid cent-precision wage or piece-rate amounts are not discarded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject modified symbolic operands in arithmetic expressions**

Fresh evidence after the finite named-operand fix shows that modifiers still bypass this list: `四万元乘以实际出勤系数`, `四万元乘以工龄系数`, and `四万元除以应出勤天数` all normalize to exact `40000.00`. A full value or cropped `四万元` candidate therefore exposes the formula's base operand as the result; recognize bounded modifier forms around these named operands, or otherwise reject explicit operators followed by symbolic factors without misclassifying words such as `加班费`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject amount-free wage-standard labels**

Extend this definite no-amount grammar to labels such as `工资标准`, `每月工资标准`, `基本工资标准`, and `今日工资标准`. They currently classify as `undetermined`, so `validateRuntimeCandidateOutput` accepts model-produced money candidates for them even though they contain neither an amount nor an unknown-amount marker, inflating accepted coverage instead of using the existing no-amount rejection path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not parse the 分 in 分钟 as currency**

Require a lexical boundary after the `分` subunit. In source text such as `王甲收到工资1000元5分钟后离开`, a candidate value `1000元5分`—or the entire narrative value—currently normalizes to exact `1000.05`, because the token stops before `钟`; runtime source review preserves that exact amount. This converts a duration into cents and can expose the wrong wage amount, so `分` must not be accepted when it begins `分钟` or another non-currency word.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a monetary second endpoint after range connectors**

Do not classify every numeral after `至`/`到` as a money-range endpoint. Because `RANGE_AFTER` checks only the first numeral, a valid `3万元` candidate in `拖欠工资3万元至2024年5月仍未支付` or `拖欠工资3万元至4个月内付清` is downgraded to `range` with no amount, even though the following number is a date or duration rather than a second monetary endpoint. Require the suffix to complete a supported monetary amount before discarding the anchored exact amount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse the supported traditional 圓 currency unit**

Include `圓` in the exact money-token grammar. The surrounding currency and range helpers already treat it as an RMB unit, so values such as `4000圓`, `四千圓`, and `人民幣四千圓` are classified as monetary but normalize to `unsupported` with no amount, while the equivalent `圆` forms normalize exactly. This causes otherwise explicit RMB wages in traditional text or OCR output to remain unavailable for review and calculation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse Chinese subunit digits after Arabic yuan**

The token grammar accepts Chinese digits in the 角/分 suffix, but this parser only accepts `\d`, so ordinary mixed literals such as `5元五角` and `5元零五分` are classified as `unsupported` instead of exact `5.50` and `5.05`. This leaves valid wage and rate amounts unavailable even though both all-Arabic and all-Chinese equivalents are supported; parse the same single-digit Chinese forms here, including the optional 零 before fen.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude lexical 角 and 分 words from the monetary gate**

Fresh evidence after the subunit-boundary fix shows that standalone non-currency expressions such as `5分鐘`, `5分米`, and `5角度` still take this `explicit` branch and are accepted by `validateRuntimeCandidateOutput` as money candidates with `amount: null`. The negative lookahead only excludes simplified `分钟` and does not reuse the lexical boundary vocabulary already used by `moneyTokenHasNonCurrencySubunit`, so these inputs inflate accepted coverage instead of entering the no-amount rejection path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore unreaped zombies when waiting for process-group shutdown**

In container environments whose PID 1 does not promptly reap orphaned grandchildren, `process.kill(-child.pid, 0)` continues succeeding after SIGKILL because the group contains only a zombie that this process cannot reap. This loop therefore always reaches the five-second error even though the descendant socket is already closed; fresh evidence from running the committed `scripts/material-facts-v7-http-process-tree.test.mjs` in the repository container is that all five lifecycle cases fail with `process group did not stop`, making the newly added mandatory `npm run check` suite fail. Detect live non-zombie members or verify the owned resources instead of requiring ESRCH.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the cancellation runner's whole process group stopped**

When a Wrangler descendant redirects its stdio and ignores SIGTERM, the parent can close and satisfy this await while that descendant remains alive; the SIGKILL branch is never entered, and this function clears `worker` without checking the detached process group. In the cancellation HTTP runner, which later restarts the Worker and eventually deletes its disposable state, that orphan can retain sockets or files and make the isolated regression flaky. Apply the group-liveness/KILL check used by the v7 runner before returning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject omitted boundary qualifiers before exact parsing**

Fresh evidence in the current tree is that qualifiers such as `不满`, `未满`, `低于`, `高于`, and `多达` are absent from this list: `normalizeMoneyValueV4('不满四万元')` returns exact `40000.00`, and a cropped `四万元` from source text `工资不满四万元` remains exact through runtime source review. This turns an upper or lower bound into a usable fixed amount, so these finite boundary forms need the same non-exact treatment as `不足` and `不低于`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject qualified ranges as exact endpoints**

When either range endpoint carries an approximation modifier, these checks no longer recognize the connector. For example, a cropped `4万元` from `工资为3万余元至4万元` or `3万元左右至4万元` survives runtime review as exact `40000.00`; similarly, `3万元` remains exact in `3万元至约4万元`. The complete expressions are already non-exact, so the source-bound endpoint grammar must allow bounded endpoint qualifiers while still requiring a monetary second endpoint.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject 成 and 折 computations around an amount**

The attached-arithmetic grammar recognizes percentages, fractions, and `倍`, but not ordinary Chinese proportion forms. Consequently, a cropped `四万元` from `四万元的八成`, `四万元的八折`, or `四万元打八折` remains exact `40000.00` through source review even though it is only the base operand; add bounded `成`/`折` forms to the arithmetic guard rather than exposing the operand as the result.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
